claim.pdf_says: The size of the current record is determined by rules specified in the RECORD clause. If the file description entry contains a RECORD IS VARYING clause, the implied move is a group move. The implied MOVE statement
claim.markdown_says: <u>The size of the current record is determined by rules specified in the RECORD clause. ║If the file description entry contains a RECORD IS VARYING clause, the implied move is a group move.</u>║ The implied MOVE statement
claim.explanation: The printed page has no underlining in this rule. The lines the transcription read as underlining are the staircase border of the change box, which starts mid-line at 'If the file description entry...' (its top edge runs over the end of the line 'The size of the current record is determined by rules', and its lower-left step runs under 'specified in the RECORD clause.'). The ║ box markers are placed correctly. The <u>...</u> markup is spurious and should be removed, which also fixes the bad nesting of </u> inside the box span.
claim.why_it_matters: Spurious underlining in prose adds emphasis the standard does not print and mis-nests with the change-box markers; it does not alter the rule text.

verdict.reasoning: Checked the 300 dpi render of page 419 (VII-45), rule (8) b. A staircase change box encloses 'If the file description entry contains a RECORD IS VARYING clause, the implied move is a group move.' Its top edge runs over the second half of the line 'The size of the current record is determined by rules'. A short vertical tick sits just before 'If', and the lower-left step runs under 'specified in the RECORD clause.' then turns down to enclose 'IS VARYING clause, ... group move.' and closes with a vertical bar before 'The implied MOVE'. Nothing outside that border is underlined: the strokes are box edges, not underscores. In the markdown (page-419.md line 25), <u> opens before 'The size of the current record', which is outside the box, and </u> closes inside the ║ span, so the nesting is wrong too. The words match exactly. The only defect is the spurious <u> markup, so cosmetic is the right severity and the claim's description is accurate.
